stem:
Lila measures a crayon on a ruler marked only in centimetres. The tip sits between the $9\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ marks.

Which two claims correctly state how she should report the length more accurately?

options.text: Report $9\,\mathrm{cm}$, because the tip has not reached $10\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Split the $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ gap into equal smaller parts and count how many the tip passes.
Those equal smaller parts of the same centimetre interval let her name a length between $9\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $10\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Treat the printed $9$ on the crayon wrapper as the measured length.

teacher.key_rationale: Between whole-centimetre marks, equal subunit parts of the same 1 cm interval give a finer length. Stopping at 9 cm alone, or reading a wrapper print, miss that measurement step.
